I have noted your symptoms of double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To determine the cause of this pattern of neurological and muscular dysfunction, I will need to ask a few questions and may order some tests.

text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pattern of weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest is very suggestive of a specific condition. Does the diplopia (double vision) ever resolve completely when you close one eye, and do you experience any slurred speech or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies and the examination finding of ptosis worsening with upward gaze, combined with your history of fluctuating weakness, are classic indicators. Do you experience significant fatigue that forces you to stop frequently when climbing stairs, and have you noticed any drooping of the eyelids during the day?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for clarifying; your denial of recent infections and family history further supports a diagnosis not caused by an infectious agent or genetics. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
